question: Can one masked-modelling encoder pre-trained on heterogeneous multi-source banking event histories plus profile state serve as a general representation layer across credit, fraud, engagement, recommendation, LTV and recurrence tasks?
hypothesis: Banking event sequences admit transferable representations in the way text and vision do, so a single pre-trained backbone (linear probe or LoRA) beats task-specific pipelines.
contributions: PRAGMA, a family of encoder-style foundation models for multi-source banking user histories, 10M to 1B parameters, with key-value-time tokenisation and a two-branch design (profile-state and event encoders feeding a history encoder).
A pre-training recipe for long irregular histories: masked modelling, sequence packing, dynamic batching; LoRA fine-tuning of the pre-trained backbone matches or beats full training from scratch.

Evaluation of one backbone on six downstream tasks (credit scoring, fraud, LTV, communication engagement, recurrent transactions, product recommendation) plus ablations, an uplift task and an AML failure case.

method.summary: Each user record (event history plus profile state, each a timestamp and key-value pairs) is tokenised into key, value and time components, encoded by a profile-state encoder, a per-event encoder and a history encoder, and pre-trained with BERT-style masking at token, event and key level. Downstream use is a frozen-embedding linear probe or LoRA fine-tuning; all results are relative deltas only.
method.task: masked-modelling pretraining of an encoder on banking event sequences; downstream binary/multi-label classification and uplift

models.name: PRAGMA-M + Nemotron-1B-v2 text encoder
models.architecture: PRAGMA-M with frozen Nemotron-1B-v2 mapping whole text value to one vector, one-layer trainable projection; MLM on text fields replaced by MSE reconstruction of the text embedding

models.name: task-specific baselines
models.architecture: null: described only as 'existing task-specific baselines' / 'production baseline' / 'internal uplift baseline'; AML baseline uses cross-record network-level features

training.objective: BERT-style MLM; cross-entropy with label smoothing; MLM head takes concat of Event Encoder token output, History Encoder [EVT] output and History Encoder [USR] output (3d projected to d) matched against embedding table. Masking: token-level 15%, event-level 10%, semantic-type (key) level 10%; a small fraction of selected positions replaced by [UNK] (no loss, acts as input dropout).
training.batch_size: dynamic batching with a fixed token budget fitting GPU memory (value not given)
training.tokens: 207 B tokens in corpus (epochs/passes not stated)
training.seq_len: up to 6,500 events per user; 24 tokens per event; 200 profile tokens
training.regularisation: label smoothing (value not given); GELU, pre-norm LayerNorm
training.hardware: S and M: 16x NVIDIA H100; L: 32x NVIDIA H100
training.wall_clock: S about 2 days; M and L each roughly 2 weeks

other.sequence packing: varlen attention kernel (Dao et al., 2022) over flat event-token buffer; 2-5x throughput vs padded baseline
other.storage: LMDB user index + Parquet event shards partitioned by event count
other.LoRA: QKV projections and MLP layers; rank 8, alpha 8 default; sweep {4, 8, 16} on smaller datasets; ~2-4% trainable params; Adam; 12 hours to a few days, about one-eighth of pre-training wall-clock
other.probe: logistic/linear regression, L-BFGS, standard-scaled embeddings; [USR], final [EVT], or both
other.positional: static sine/cosine within-field positions; RoPE over log-seconds for profile and history encoders; calendar features (hour of day, day of week, day of month) as sin/cos through 2 MLP layers added to event embedding

inference.samples: null: runs, seeds and confidence intervals not stated

other.serving: PRAGMA reads a user's recent events from a shared event bus with relaxed delivery guarantees; staleness test drops recent events within a window equal to the 99.9th percentile of propagation delays. No latency or throughput figures given.

limits: Absolute metrics withheld as commercially sensitive; every result is a relative delta (x/baseline - 1)%, so no result can be reproduced or placed on a common scale.
Baselines are internal, unnamed 'task-specific' production models; their architecture, features and tuning are not described, so gains of +130% PR-AUC cannot be interpreted.
Data, code and weights not released; no licence stated in the text.
No operating points, thresholds or alert rates for fraud; only relative precision and recall.
No online or A/B results; evaluation is offline only. Serving is described only in terms of event staleness (no latency or cost numbers).
No seeds, variances, confidence intervals or significance tests; the non-monotone scaling in comm. engagement ROC-AUC (+19.6/+17.4/+20.4) is within unknown noise.
Pre-training split (temporal or by user) and downstream dataset sizes not stated; downstream folds are 'pre-defined'.
Scratch comparison is only at PRAGMA-M; no model-size scaling law or data-scaling ablation; no masking-variant ablation (the three masking types are not ablated).
Learning rate, schedule, warmup, batch size and steps not given.
Authors concede AML is a failure: isolated per-record embeddings miss cross-record network structure. Text encoder variant adds about 18% training latency and hurts product rec.
Authors are Revolut and NVIDIA employees; results are company-internal.
